action.description: Form submit / Enter, send/post click, upload, … (policy is the core's).

chain.description: Delegation chain from the surface thread to the asking thread.

order.description: Per-surface presentation order; the lowest is the active card (P §8.5).

surfaceThreadId.description: Top-level chat that shows a sub-agent's request.

oneOf.description: Removes every init script of the page (the old init_script `clear`).

BrowserScreenshotClip.description: The region a screenshot is cut to: an element a snapshot ref names, or a rectangle in CSS pixels.

chain.description: Delegation chain from the surface thread to the asking thread.

order.description: Per-surface presentation order; the lowest is the active card (P §8.5).

surfaceThreadId.description: Top-level chat that shows a sub-agent's request.

EmulationSpec.description: The overrides of the `emulate` command (`browser/emulation-validation.ts`); the host merges them with the pane viewport.

FrameRef.description: A frame of a page: a child session and/or a frame id; absent means the main frame.

HostBrowserCdpSendParams.description: `host/browser/cdp/send`: refused with -32015 for the methods in `BROWSER_ENGINE_CDP_REFUSED`.

HostBrowserInputBatchParams.description: `host/browser/input/batch`: the steps run in order; the batch stops at a dialog.

HostBrowserLiveControlParams.description: Params of `host/browser/liveControl` (core → host): a live-view control that is not page input. The page input itself goes as `host/browser/command{action:"input"}`. The result is null; a failure is a JSON-RPC error.

HostBrowserPagesResolveParams.description: `host/browser/pages/resolve` (core to host): the page a session's command works on, opened or adopted when needed.

HostBrowserPagesSurfaceParams.description: `host/browser/pages/surface`: show, hide or hand off the pane (the host also sends `host/browser/surface`).

saveTrace.description: Save the redacted trace in the host's own trace folder (the old `saveTrace`); `export_path` names another absolute folder instead.

HostBrowserRefCallParams.description: `host/browser/ref/call`: a function called on the element a snapshot ref names.

HostCommandParams.description: Params of `host/browser/command` (core → host): a browser action on the pages of `threadId`, with its input. The host answers with the action's result, which may carry the desktop's `BrowserCommandTiming` as `timing`, or fails it with the JSON-RPC error -32000, whose message is already redacted and whose `data.timing` is the failed command's `BrowserCommandTiming`. Both timings are diagnostics: the core writes them to its agent trace (`browser_timing` rows) and never shows them to the model.

HostComputerAppInputParams.description: Params of `host/computer/appInput` (core -> host): input into one of the desktop's own windows, delivered through its renderer without OS focus or the pointer. The desktop answers -32602 when `windowId` is not app-owned. A member an `op` does not use is absent.

modifiers.description: `wheel`: the modifiers held while it turns, e.g. `ctrl+shift`.

x.description: `click`, `move`, `wheel`: physical pixels relative to the window's bounds.

HostComputerCaptureParams.description: Params of `host/computer/capture` (core → host): the `capture` command exactly as the loopback bridge was posted it (`computer-bridge/client.mjs`: the host command plus `session_id`).

HostComputerCommandParams.description: Params of `host/computer/command` (core -> host, dual path only): a whole bridge command, as `computer-bridge/client.mjs` posts it. Answered only while the desktop runs the legacy Windows PowerShell host.

HostComputerCursorPrepareParams.description: Params of `host/computer/cursorPrepare` (core -> host): ready the agent's arrow before the first pointer input of a session. The desktop answers within 750 ms (`overlay/cursor-readiness.ts`); the core waits at most 900 ms and goes on without it.

HostComputerForegroundLeaseParams.description: Params of `host/computer/foregroundLease` (core → host): one foreground-lock request of a Computer Use helper. Windows lets only a process that may set the foreground take the lock, which while the user works in a Mixdog window is the desktop, so the core relays the request there (`foreground-lock-host.ts` `handle`). A number the op does not use is 0.

action.description: The helper's request in flight that asks, 1..2^31-1.

answerBy.description: `acquire`: when the helper stops waiting for the answer, in ms on QueryPerformanceCounter.

holdMs.description: `acquire`: the longest the lock may be held, 1..1000 ms.

instance.description: The helper that asks: the core's id for it, never reused (`LeaseWorker.instance`).

lease.description: `release`: the lease it ends; 0 when the helper was told none.

seq.description: The ask's number within that request, 1..2^31-1.

HostComputerLeaseOp.description: What a `host/computer/foregroundLease` request does (`foreground-lock-host.ts` `LeaseThreadRequest`): `acquire` and `release` relay a helper's `@@MIXDOG_FGLOCK@@` line; `gone` says the helper exited, so a lease it holds ends now (`workerGone`).

HostComputerPermissionsParams.description: Params of `host/computer/permissions` (core -> host): `request` asks macOS to show its own prompts (`requestComputerPermissions`) before the grants are read; absent or false only reads.

HostComputerPixelsBackend.description: How the pixels of `host/computer/pixels` are taken.

HostComputerPixelsParams.description: Params of `host/computer/pixels` (core -> host): one capture, encoded by the desktop, which uploads the bytes with `blob/put` before it answers. Replaces `host/computer/capture` for display and app-owned pixels. Errors are -32000 with `data.code` `computer_capture_unavailable`, `computer_capture_permission` or `computer_window_gone`.

region.description: The part of the display to capture, in physical pixels of the screen (the display's origin included): the core's display zoom asks for the region at full resolution and answers `source` with the rectangle delivered, which must equal the region. Absent = the whole display (g25-fu-cu-b, s3-10).

HostComputerPixelsRegion.description: A rectangle of a display in physical pixels of the screen.

oneOf.description: A display to capture: by id, by index, or (both absent) the primary one.
A window to capture, named as the helper names windows (`hwnd:0x..`, `cg:<n>`, `x11:0x..`).

HostComputerPointerFeedbackParams.description: Params of `host/computer/pointerFeedback` (core → host): a helper's pointer progress, which the overlay draws as the agent's arrow. Each event is a `@@MIXDOG_POINTER@@` line the core checked against the request it belongs to (`worker-pool.ts` `reportPointerProgress`). The host answers `null`.

events.description: In the helper's order, each with what `publishPointerProgress` takes: `x`, `y`, `held`, `phase`, `mode` and `windowId`.

HostFileSnapshotParams.description: Params of `host/capture/fileSnapshot` (core → host). The core has already confined the path.

HostFilesTrashItemParams.description: Params of `host/files/trashItem` (core → host): the absolute path the core has already confined.

HostLocalPageUrlParams.description: Params of `host/localPage/url` (core → host); the result is the URL string.

confirmed.description: Node's `updaterInstall` argument `args[0]`: the user confirmed the install.

HostVisualizeCommandParams.description: Params of `host/visualize/command` (core → host): the loopback bridge's request body. The result is the service's object (`{text, tabs?, path?, …}`), `null` when it returns nothing (`visualizeCommand`: `(await visualize.command(…)) ?? null`).

HostWindowOpenParams.description: `host/window/open`: opens (or focuses) the window of a server.

InterceptRule.description: One intercept rule (`browser/intercept.ts` `BrowserInterceptRule`); `id` and `hits` are the host's, absent on an `add`.

LiveControlKind.description: What `host/browser/liveControl` carries to the viewed page.

oneOf.description: A phone's `resize-request`: `request` is its `resize` object (`{mode: "page"}` or `{mode: "fit-client", cssWidth, cssHeight, deviceScaleFactor}`); the host resizes the page (Node's `remote.resize(sessionId, request)`).
A phone's `ready.videoLimit`: `request` is `{maxWidth, maxHeight}`; the host may capture larger than its frame bound, up to it, and lock a new geometry (Node's `remote.widenVideo(sessionId, limit)`).

LocalPageScope.description: What a `host/localPage/url` lease covers; absent means `project`.

ModelProxyExecuteParams.description: Server core → a connection with `capabilities.modelProxy`: run one model call with this machine's accounts. Completion is the response; losing the connection resolves the call `cancelled`.

chain.description: Delegation chain from the surface thread to the asking thread.

order.description: Per-surface presentation order; the lowest is the active card (P §8.5).

surfaceThreadId.description: Top-level chat that shows a sub-agent's request.

Precondition.description: The page state a mutating call was decided against; the host checks it synchronously right before the CDP send and refuses with -32010 when it no longer holds.

ProxyBinary.description: A file part's bytes. The sender's attachment-store reference means nothing on the PC, so it is never carried: the sender inlines the bytes (under its byte budget), and a reference that stays travels as `unavailable`.

ProxyCall.description: What the remote runtime asks of the PC's providers (`ModelProxyProvider`, `quota-reading.mjs:93`, `loadModelProxyProviderConfig`).

oneOf.description: `listModels`; `refresh` re-reads the provider first (`_refreshModelCache`).

updates.description: `(message index, effort)` pairs; a JSON object would key them by text.

accountRouting.description: The account that served this answer, as the server kept it from the run's `accountRouting` event (Node `providerMetadata.accountRouting`): the PC's pool reads it back from the history to keep the conversation on that account.

ProxyOptions.description: `RequestOptions` field for field. The connection scope and the model's output ceiling are the PC's to derive, so they are not carried.

forkedTransportScope.description: The server forked this request from a session (a side question) and gave it a transport scope of its own (`options.transportScope`). Its string means nothing on this PC, which allocates a scope for the request and releases it when the request ends.

agent.description: An agent/tool session, or a send carrying tools.

legacy.description: A session that predates the wire table (`model-proxy-provider.mjs:193`).

ScreenDisplaysParams.description: Params of `browser/screenDisplays` (a granted phone's request, Node's `browserRemoteScreenDisplays`) and of `host/screen/displays` (core → host): none. Both answer `RemoteScreenDisplaySummary[]` (`apps/desktop/src/shared/remote-webrtc.ts`), unchanged.

oneOf.description: Human-in-the-loop gate (R41): response values of `ToolApprovalDecision.response`.

chain.description: Delegation chain from the surface thread to the asking thread.

order.description: Per-surface presentation order; the lowest is the active card (P §8.5).

request.description: The card content (tool input, editable fields, reason).

description: Request from the core to a client.

`ask_user` questions, including room hand-off questions.
Raised by the core's browser policy; any eligible client presents it.

The accessibility snapshot of a page.

Dispatch a batch of keyboard and pointer steps.

Send an allowlisted CDP command through the host's fenced executor.

Read or change a page's local or session storage.

Start or stop a performance trace, or read metrics.

List or take a session's downloads.
Put files into a file input, chooser, drop target or picker.
The displays of this PC's screen, for the phone's remote-screen picker.
A Computer Use screen capture, taken and encoded by the desktop's computer host.
The displays of this PC as the computer host reports them.

The desktop's own Computer Use windows, which the core leaves out of every window list.
A Computer Use helper's pointer progress, for the overlay's arrow.

The desktop's own windows a session may read and drive.
Input into one of the desktop's own windows through its renderer.

This PC's notification support and system idle time, which decides whether paired devices hold their pushes (Node's host method `notificationStatus`).

Opens (or focuses) the window of a server (`showConnectionWindow`); `opened` is false when the window could not be made.
